classCriteria.description: The system installs and evaluates controls inside or against a target repository.
The system governs multiple software-delivery lifecycle activities rather than one isolated command.
The system requires structured evidence, evaluates gates, and can reject unsupported completion claims.
The system wraps external coding-agent execution with repository controls, adapters, evidence, and verification instead of replacing that runtime.
The system itself reads, edits, and implements the target code as the responsible coding runtime.
The system coordinates defined policy, state, gates, and evidence around external coding-agent work, which supports a qualified secondary control-plane description.

sourcedFacts: ASD-STE100 is a formal controlled natural language with writing rules and a controlled dictionary.
W3C describes ontologies as formalized domain vocabularies that define terms through relationships.
NIST describes SSDF as practices integrated into SDLC implementations.
Kubernetes uses control plane for components that manage overall cluster state.
Anthropic and GitHub assign repository inspection and code-changing responsibilities to external coding-agent tools.
inferences: Valdris is best classified as a repository-level SDLC assurance harness for AI coding agents because it surrounds external implementation work with repository controls, routing, evidence, and gates.
The selected category is an emerging descriptive compound, not a formal class defined by the cited standards.
Valdris has a qualified secondary role as a repository-level policy and evidence control plane around external coding agents.
